question: If a constant current of 2 A is maintained in a conductor of resistance 100 Ω, then the potential difference across the conductor is:
solution:
The correct answer is __**200V.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• To find the potential difference across a conductor when a constant current is maintained, we can use Ohm's Law, which is given by the formula:
 
 
• V=I×R
 
 
 
• Where,​
 
 
• V = Potential Difference (Voltage)
 
• I I" id="MathJax-Element-3-Frame" role="presentation" style="position: relative;" tabindex="0">II I" id="MathJax-Element-22-Frame" role="presentation" style="position: relative;" tabindex="0">II I" id="MathJax-Element-38-Frame" role="presentation" style="position: relative;" tabindex="0">II I I I I I I II = Current = 2 A
 
• R R" id="MathJax-Element-4-Frame" role="presentation" style="position: relative;" tabindex="0">RR R" id="MathJax-Element-23-Frame" role="presentation" style="position: relative;" tabindex="0">RR R" id="MathJax-Element-39-Frame" role="presentation" style="position: relative;" tabindex="0">RR R R R R R R RR = Resistance = 100 Ω
 
 
 
• Substituting the given values into the formula
 
 
• V=2A×100Ω=200V
 
 
 
• Therefore, the potential difference across the conductor is **200 volts (V)**.
